O.P.

i got cable installed yesterday, and i noticed the techie used a cd to install the bigpond login program onto my computer. I asked him before he left if i could get a copy of the cd with the login program on it.... however no luck. he told me that it is called config w or something.

i was wondering if there is anywhere on the net where i can get this program from?

any help would be greatly appreciated.

he was supposed to leave you a copy of the cd aswell as a welcome pack booklet with your login and account info on the inside cover. Ring Telstra and complain and the guy will bring one back. Also check that he left you with all the cables that came with the modem that arent used. (a uSB connection and/or a RG45 ethernet cable. Some techs keep em to stock up there own collection and sell them at the markets or their local Charlie Chan computer store.

There shoudl be a link to the program somewhere on the bigpond site.

Otherwise go to ftp://update-server and somewhere in there is the login program. You can access that ftp without being logged onto bigpond. Helpfull if you've just formatted :)

But ive been using BPALogin for 3 years and it hasn't failed me yet :)

bpalogin.sourceforge.net

</div></td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.65em;"><div style="display: inline-block; line-height: 1.2em; padding: .1em 0; white-space: normal;">Running time</div></th><td class="infobox-data">99 minutes</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.65em;">Country</th><td class="infobox-data">United States</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.65em;">Language</th><td class="infobox-data">English</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.65em;">Budget</th><td class="infobox-data">$6.2 million</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" class="infobox-label" style="white-space: nowrap; padding-right: 0.65em;">Box office</th><td class="infobox-data">$63.5 million<sup id="cite_ref-Risky_Business_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Risky_Business-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><i><b>Risky Business</b></i> is a 1983 American <a href="/wiki/Coming-of-age_story" title="Coming-of-age story">coming-of-age</a> <a href="/wiki/Teen_film" title="Teen film">teen</a> <a href="/wiki/Comedy_film" title="Comedy film">comedy film</a>  written and directed by <a href="/wiki/Paul_Brickman" title="Paul Brickman">Paul Brickman</a> (in his directorial debut) and starring <a href="/wiki/Tom_Cruise" title="Tom Cruise">Tom Cruise</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rebecca_De_Mornay" title="Rebecca De Mornay">Rebecca De Mornay</a>. It follows the sexual exploits of high school senior Joel Goodson (Cruise), who is staying home alone during his parents' <a href="/wiki/Vacation" title="Vacation">vacation</a> trip and meets a <a href="/wiki/Call_girl" title="Call girl">call girl</a> named Lana (De Mornay). The film is considered to be Cruise's <a href="/wiki/Breakthrough_role" title="Breakthrough role">breakout role</a>.
</p><p><i>Risky Business</i> was released theatrically in the United States on August 5, 1983. A commercial and critical success, the film grossed more than $63 million at the box office, making it the <a href="/wiki/1983_in_film" title="1983 in film">tenth-highest-grossing film of 1983 in the United States</a>, and received acclaim, with many comparing it to <i><a href="/wiki/The_Graduate" title="The Graduate">The Graduate</a></i> (1967). Cruise's performance earned him the first <a href="/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards" title="Golden Globe Awards">Golden Globe Award</a> nomination of his career.
</p><p>Retrospective critical analysis has recognized <i>Risky Business</i> as one of the best <a href="/wiki/Teen_film" title="Teen film">high school and teen films</a> of all time.
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc">
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Plot">Plot</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Plot"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>High-achieving high school student Joel Goodson lives with his wealthy parents in the <a href="/wiki/North_Shore_(Chicago)" title="North Shore (Chicago)">Chicago North Shore</a> area of <a href="/wiki/Glencoe,_Illinois" title="Glencoe, Illinois">Glencoe</a>. His father wants him to attend <a href="/wiki/Princeton_University" title="Princeton University">Princeton University</a>, his <i>alma mater</i>, so Joel participates in Future Enterprisers, an extracurricular activity in which students work in teams to create small businesses. When Joel's parents go away on a trip, his friend Miles convinces him to use his newfound freedom to have some fun. On the first night, Joel raids the liquor cabinet, plays the stereo loudly, and dances around the living room in his briefs and button-down shirt to "<a href="/wiki/Old_Time_Rock_and_Roll" title="Old Time Rock and Roll">Old Time Rock and Roll</a>".
</p><p>The following day, Miles calls a prostitute named Jackie on Joel's behalf. Jackie turns out to be a male <a href="/wiki/Cross-dressing" title="Cross-dressing">cross-dresser</a>, so Joel pays him just to leave. But, as he is leaving, he gives Joel the number for another prostitute, Lana. That night, Joel is unable to sleep and hesitantly calls Lana, who is revealed as a gorgeous blonde woman, and they spend the entire night having sex.
</p><p>The next morning, Lana asks Joel for $300 ($925 in 2023 dollars) for her services. He goes to the bank, but when he returns, she is gone, along with his mother's expensive <a href="/wiki/Steuben_Glass_Works" title="Steuben Glass Works">Steuben glass egg</a>. Joel finds Lana and demands the egg back, but her pimp <a href="/wiki/Guido_(slang)" title="Guido (slang)">Guido</a> interrupts them, pulling a gun. While in his father's <a href="/wiki/Porsche_928" title="Porsche 928">Porsche 928</a>, Joel is chased by Guido, but eventually escapes. Lana tells Joel that the egg is with the rest of her belongings at Guido's. He lets her stay at his house while he goes to school. When he returns, his friends have come over, and Lana has invited another prostitute, Vicki, to stay, but Joel rejects the idea. The women leave, only to encounter Guido and get into an altercation on Joel's front lawn before running back into his house. Joel agrees to the women spending one more night.
</p><p>Later that night, Joel, Lana, Vicki, and Joel's friend Barry go out and get high on marijuana. After Lana accidentally bumps the Porsche out of gear while retrieving her purse, the car rolls down the hill and onto a pier (despite Joel's desperate attempt to stop it); the pier collapses, and the Porsche sinks into <a href="/wiki/Lake_Michigan" title="Lake Michigan">Lake Michigan</a>. When Joel takes the car to a repair shop, he is horrified to learn how much fixing it will cost. He and Lana later decide to turn his parents' house into a brothel for a night; Joel's share of the profits will pay for the repairs. The party is hugely successful; the house is packed with Joel's friends and classmates and Lana's co-workers. However, the recruiter from Princeton, Rutherford, chooses that night to interview Joel for admission to Princeton. The interview is plagued by interruptions, and Rutherford is unimpressed by Joel's résumé. Afterwards, he stays at the party and becomes acquainted with Lana's friends. After the party, Joel and Lana make love on a <a href="/wiki/Chicago_%22L%22" title="Chicago "L"">Chicago "L"</a> train.
</p><p>The next morning, when Joel comes home after retrieving his father's car from the repair shop, he finds that his house has been burglarized. When he tries to call Lana, Guido answers; he tells him he will let Joel buy back his furniture. Joel and his friends manage to get everything moved back in just as his parents walk in, though his mother notices a crack in her egg. Later, Joel's father congratulates him; the interviewer was very impressed, and Joel will be accepted into Princeton.
</p><p>Joel meets Lana at a restaurant, and they speculate about their future. She tells him that she wants to keep on seeing him; he jokes that it will cost her.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Production">Production</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Production"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Sean_Penn" title="Sean Penn">Sean Penn</a> (who portrayed Jeff Spicoli in the previous year's <i><a href="/wiki/Fast_Times_at_Ridgemont_High" title="Fast Times at Ridgemont High">Fast Times at Ridgemont High</a></i>, another iconic teen film), <a href="/wiki/Gary_Sinise" title="Gary Sinise">Gary Sinise</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kevin_Bacon" title="Kevin Bacon">Kevin Bacon</a>, <a href="/wiki/John_Cusack" title="John Cusack">John Cusack</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tom_Hanks" title="Tom Hanks">Tom Hanks</a> all auditioned for the role of Joel Goodson.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-At_20,_'Risky'_is_still_frisky_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-At_20,_'Risky'_is_still_frisky-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Michelle_Pfeiffer" title="Michelle Pfeiffer">Michelle Pfeiffer</a> was offered the role of Lana, but  turned it down.<sup id="cite_ref-At_20,_'Risky'_is_still_frisky_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-At_20,_'Risky'_is_still_frisky-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Soundtrack">Soundtrack</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Soundtrack"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1236090951"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Risky_Business_(soundtrack)" title="Risky Business (soundtrack)">Risky Business (soundtrack)</a></div>
<p>The film was scored by <a href="/wiki/Tangerine_Dream" title="Tangerine Dream">Tangerine Dream</a>. Their music comprises nearly half of the soundtrack album. Also included are songs by <a href="/wiki/Muddy_Waters" title="Muddy Waters">Muddy Waters</a>, <a href="/wiki/Prince_(musician)" title="Prince (musician)">Prince</a> ("<a href="/wiki/1999_(Prince_album)" title="1999 (Prince album)">DMSR</a>"), <a href="/wiki/Jeff_Beck" title="Jeff Beck">Jeff Beck</a>, <a href="/wiki/Journey_(band)" title="Journey (band)">Journey</a>, <a href="/wiki/Phil_Collins" title="Phil Collins">Phil Collins</a> ("<a href="/wiki/In_the_Air_Tonight" title="In the Air Tonight">In the Air Tonight</a>"), and the song for which the film is best known, "<a href="/wiki/Old_Time_Rock_and_Roll" title="Old Time Rock and Roll">Old Time Rock and Roll</a>" by <a href="/wiki/Bob_Seger" title="Bob Seger">Bob Seger</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AllMusic_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AllMusic-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The soundtrack album was released on <a href="/wiki/Virgin_Records" title="Virgin Records">Virgin Records</a>, Tangerine Dream's <a href="/wiki/Tangerine_Dream_discography#The_Virgin_Years" title="Tangerine Dream discography">record company at the time</a> of the film's release.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2019)">citation needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p><p>The film also includes "<a href="/wiki/Hungry_Heart" title="Hungry Heart">Hungry Heart</a>" by <a href="/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen" title="Bruce Springsteen">Bruce Springsteen</a>, "<a href="/wiki/Every_Breath_You_Take" title="Every Breath You Take">Every Breath You Take</a>" by <a href="/wiki/The_Police" title="The Police">The Police</a>, and "Swamp" by <a href="/wiki/Talking_Heads" title="Talking Heads">Talking Heads</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/LP_album" class="mw-redirect" title="LP album">LP</a> and <a href="/wiki/CD" class="mw-redirect" title="CD">CD</a> versions of the soundtrack include two different versions of "Love on a Real Train (Risky Business)," both of which are different recordings from the version used in the film for the final love scene or closing credits.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2019)">citation needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Release">Release</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Release"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><i>Risky Business</i> premiered in New York and Los Angeles on August 5, 1983.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Home_media">Home media</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Home media"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The film was first released DVD on August 20, 1997, and on Blu-ray by <a href="/wiki/Warner_Bros." title="Warner Bros.">Warner Bros.</a> in 2008. Extra features included <a href="/wiki/Audio_commentary" title="Audio commentary">audio commentary</a> with the director and Cruise, a <a href="/wiki/Featurette" title="Featurette">featurette</a> titled The Dream Is Always the Same: The Story of “Risky Business”, an alternate ending, screen tests and trailer.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<a href="/wiki/The_Criterion_Collection" title="The Criterion Collection">The Criterion Collection</a> released the film on <a href="/wiki/4K_Ultra_HD" class="mw-redirect" title="4K Ultra HD">4K Ultra HD</a> and <a href="/wiki/Blu-ray" title="Blu-ray">Blu-ray</a> disc on July 23, 2024, with a new 4K digital restoration of both the director's cut and original theatrical release, with bonus material from the 2008 Blu-ray release. New special features include interviews with Avnet and casting director Nancy Klopper and a conversation between editor Richard Chew and film historian Bobbie O’Steen.<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Reception">Reception</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Reception"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Box_office">Box office</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: Box office"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The film opened in 670 theaters, with an opening weekend gross of $4,275,327. It went on to gross a total of $63.5 million domestically.<sup id="cite_ref-Risky_Business_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Risky_Business-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Critical_response">Critical response</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: Critical response"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><i>Risky Business</i> is considered by many critics as one of the best films of 1983.<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<a href="/wiki/Janet_Maslin" title="Janet Maslin">Janet Maslin</a>, in her 1983 review of the film for <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i>, called it "part satire, part would-be suburban poetry and part shameless showing off" and said the film "shows an abundance of style", though "you would be hard pressed to find a film whose hero's problems are of less concern to the world at large."<sup id="cite_ref-Maslin_NYT_12-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Maslin_NYT-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> She called De Mornay "disarming as a call girl who looks more like a college girl" and credits Cruise with making "Joel's transformation from straight arrow to entrepreneur about as credible as it can be made".<sup id="cite_ref-Maslin_NYT_12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Maslin_NYT-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>
The film holds a 93% rating on the review aggregate website <a href="/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes" title="Rotten Tomatoes">Rotten Tomatoes</a> based on 54 reviews, with an average of 7.3/10, with the site's consensus stating; "Featuring one of Tom Cruise's best early performances, <i>Risky Business</i> is a sharp, funny examination of teen angst that doesn't stop short of exploring dark themes".<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Roger_Ebert" title="Roger Ebert">Roger Ebert</a>'s review was positive, calling it a film of: <style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1244412712">.mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}</style></p><blockquote class="templatequote"><p>New faces and inspired insights and genuine laughs... one of the smartest, funniest, most perceptive satires in a long time... not only invites comparison with <i><a href="/wiki/The_Graduate" title="The Graduate">The Graduate</a></i>, it earns it.<sup id="cite_ref-EbertR-CST-RB_14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EbertR-CST-RB-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>—The very best thing about the movie is its dialogue. Paul Brickman, who wrote and directed, has an ear so good that he knows what to leave out. This is one of those movies where a few words or a single line says everything that needs to be said, implies everything that needs to be implied, and gets a laugh. When the hooker tells the kid, 'Oh, Joel, go to school, go <i>learn</i> something,' the precise inflection of those words defines their relationship for the next three scenes.</p></blockquote>
<p><a href="/wiki/Variety_(magazine)" title="Variety (magazine)"><i>Variety</i></a> said the film was like a "promising first novel, with all the pros and cons that come with that territory" and complimented Brickman on "the stylishness and talent of his direction".<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Legacy">Legacy</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Risky_Business&action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section: Legacy"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The remastered 25th-anniversary edition offers "both the upbeat studio ending and Mr. Brickman's original, more tentative and melancholic conclusion".<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2015 the film was #31 on <i><a href="/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly" title="Entertainment Weekly">Entertainment Weekly</a></i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">'</span>s list of the 50 Best High School Movies. The magazine called the film a "sharp satire of privileged suburban teens", portraying the "soul-crushing pressure to be perfect."<sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In the years since the film's release, the iconic scene featuring Cruise's character sliding across the floor, dancing in just his pink shirt, socks, and white briefs to <a href="/wiki/Bob_Seger" title="Bob Seger">Bob Seger</a>'s rendition of "Old Time Rock and Roll" has been recreated in episodes of many television series, as well as in films, parodies, <a href="/wiki/Viral_video" title="Viral video">viral videos</a> and advertisements. The song was #100 on <a href="/wiki/AFI%27s_100_Years_..._100_Songs" class="mw-redirect" title="AFI's 100 Years ... 100 Songs">AFI's 100 Years ... 100 Songs</a> list.
</p>

BlockFi Login: Complete Guide to Secure Account Access and Setup

BlockFi has established itself as a prominent platform in the cryptocurrency ecosystem, offering users the ability to earn interest on their digital assets. Understanding the BlockFi login process and implementing robust security measures is essential for protecting your valuable cryptocurrency investments. This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about accessing your BlockFi account securely while exploring best practices for cryptocurrency storage.

Visit Official BlockFi Website →

Understanding BlockFi Login Setup

The BlockFi login process begins with creating a secure account on the platform. Users must provide valid identification and complete the verification process to comply with regulatory requirements. The setup involves registering with your email address, creating a strong password, and enabling two-factor authentication (2FA) for enhanced security. This multi-layered approach ensures that only authorized individuals can access your account and manage your cryptocurrency holdings.

When setting up your BlockFi login credentials, it's crucial to use a unique, complex password that combines uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Password managers can help generate and store these credentials securely. Never share your login information with anyone, and be cautious of phishing attempts that may try to steal your credentials through fake websites or emails.

Cold Storage for Crypto: Maximum Security for Your Assets

While BlockFi provides institutional-grade security for assets held on their platform, understanding cold storage is essential for comprehensive cryptocurrency security. Cold storage refers to keeping your cryptocurrency completely offline, disconnected from the internet, which eliminates the risk of online hacking attempts. This method is considered the gold standard for long-term cryptocurrency storage, particularly for significant holdings of Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Cold storage solutions range from paper wallets to hardware wallets, with hardware wallets being the most user-friendly and secure option for most investors. These devices store your private keys offline while allowing you to make transactions when needed. The concept is simple: if your private keys never touch an internet-connected device, hackers cannot access them remotely.

Offline Crypto Storage: Protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum

Offline crypto storage involves keeping your digital assets in a wallet that has never been exposed to internet connectivity. For Bitcoin and Ethereum holders, this approach provides peace of mind against cyber threats, exchange hacks, and unauthorized access. Many experienced cryptocurrency investors follow the principle of keeping only the assets they actively trade on exchanges while storing the majority in cold storage.

Security Tip: Consider splitting your cryptocurrency portfolio between hot wallets (for trading and daily use) and cold storage (for long-term holdings). A common approach is keeping 10-20% in accessible wallets and 80-90% in cold storage.

Protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum through offline storage requires careful setup and backup procedures. When creating a cold storage solution, you'll receive a recovery seed phrase—typically 12 to 24 words—that can restore your wallet if the device is lost or damaged. Store this seed phrase in multiple secure physical locations, never digitally, and consider using metal backup solutions that are fire and water-resistant.

Best Hardware Wallet Security Practices

Hardware wallets represent the best balance between security and usability for cryptocurrency storage. Leading hardware wallet manufacturers like Ledger and Trezor offer devices that generate and store private keys in a secure chip, isolated from your computer or smartphone. When selecting a hardware wallet, purchase directly from the manufacturer to avoid tampered devices.

Best hardware wallet security involves several key practices. First, initialize your device in a private setting where no cameras or other people can observe your seed phrase. Second, verify the authenticity of the device through the manufacturer's security checks. Third, regularly update your device firmware to patch any discovered vulnerabilities. Fourth, test your recovery process with small amounts before trusting the device with significant holdings.

Important Notice: Never enter your hardware wallet seed phrase into any website, software application, or digital device. Legitimate services will never ask for your complete seed phrase. This is the most common method scammers use to steal cryptocurrency.

Integration between BlockFi and hardware wallets allows you to maintain control of your private keys while still utilizing platform services when desired. Understanding how to securely transfer assets between your BlockFi account and cold storage is crucial for a comprehensive security strategy.

Securing Your BlockFi Login Experience

Beyond basic password protection, securing your BlockFi login involves enabling all available security features. Two-factor authentication using an authenticator app (rather than SMS) provides stronger protection against SIM-swapping attacks. BlockFi also offers withdrawal whitelisting, which restricts withdrawals to pre-approved addresses, adding another layer of security.

Learn More About BlockFi Security Features →

Regular monitoring of your account activity helps detect unauthorized access attempts early. Set up email and mobile notifications for all account activities, including logins from new devices, withdrawal requests, and profile changes. If you notice any suspicious activity, change your password immediately and contact BlockFi support.

Best Practices for Cryptocurrency Asset Management

Successful cryptocurrency management combines the convenience of platforms like BlockFi with the security of cold storage. Develop a clear strategy for how you'll divide your holdings: keep actively traded amounts or assets earning interest on BlockFi, while maintaining your long-term holdings in cold storage. This approach maximizes both utility and security.

Regularly review and update your security practices as the cryptocurrency landscape evolves. Stay informed about new threats, security features, and best practices through official channels and reputable cryptocurrency security resources. Remember that you are your own bank in the cryptocurrency world—the responsibility for security ultimately rests with you.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1: How do I set up my BlockFi login for the first time?
To set up your BlockFi login, visit the official BlockFi website and click "Sign Up." Provide your email address, create a strong password, and complete the identity verification process. Enable two-factor authentication immediately after account creation for enhanced security. You'll need to provide government-issued ID and pass KYC verification before you can start using the platform's services.
Q2: What is cold storage and why is it important for cryptocurrency?
Cold storage refers to keeping your cryptocurrency private keys completely offline, disconnected from the internet. This is important because it eliminates the risk of online hacking, malware, and remote theft. Cold storage is especially recommended for long-term holdings and large amounts of cryptocurrency, as it provides the highest level of security available.
Q3: Which hardware wallet offers the best security for Bitcoin and Ethereum?
Leading hardware wallets like Ledger Nano X, Ledger Nano S Plus, and Trezor Model T all offer excellent security for Bitcoin and Ethereum. The best choice depends on your specific needs—Ledger devices offer Bluetooth connectivity and support for more cryptocurrencies, while Trezor devices are fully open-source. All reputable hardware wallets use secure element chips and require physical confirmation for transactions.
Q4: Can I use BlockFi and cold storage together?
Yes, many users employ a hybrid strategy using both BlockFi and cold storage. Keep the cryptocurrency you want to actively trade or earn interest on within your BlockFi account, while storing long-term holdings in cold storage via a hardware wallet. This approach balances convenience with security, allowing you to benefit from BlockFi's services while maintaining ultimate control over your primary holdings.
Q5: What should I do if I forget my BlockFi login password?
If you forget your BlockFi login password, click the "Forgot Password" link on the login page. You'll receive a password reset link via email. For security reasons, always use the official BlockFi website or mobile app for password resets. Never click on password reset links from unsolicited emails, as these could be phishing attempts. After resetting, enable two-factor authentication if you haven't already.
Q6: How often should I transfer crypto from BlockFi to cold storage?
The frequency of transfers depends on your investment strategy and the amounts involved. A common approach is to move significant accumulations to cold storage quarterly or when your hot wallet balance exceeds a predetermined threshold (such as 10-20% of your total holdings). Consider the transaction fees and your security needs when deciding on transfer frequency. For very large holdings, immediate transfer to cold storage after purchase is recommended.
